metadata.description: DSH Web GUI: attach a long-running job id to a conversation and let its sidebar row carry the state -- pink while it runs, green when it finished (come back and analyse), amber when the id cannot be found. Providers are a command + a per-line regex. Not affiliated with DeepSeek.
metadata.name: dsh-job-watch

paragraphs.text: DSH Web GUI: attach a long-running job id to a conversation and let its sidebar row carry the state
-- pink while it runs, green when it finished (come back and analyse), amber when the id cannot be f
ound. Providers are a command + a per-line regex. Not affiliated with DeepSeek.
# dsh-job-watch

**A long-running job you did not start, pinned to the conversation that cares about it.**
The sideba

r row of that conversation turns **pink** while the job runs, **green** once it has
finished (come b
ack and analyse the result), and **amber** when the job id cannot be found.
English | 中文速览

> **Not affiliated with DeepSeek.** This is an independent community plugin for
> DeepSeek Harness (

DSH). "DeepSeek Harness" is named
> only to describe compatibility.
## The problem
An agent submits a job that takes six hours — to a cluster scheduler, to a bare-metal box over SSH,

to
`tmux` somewhere — and then the session goes quiet. The job's state lives in a completely differe

nt program
(`squeue`, `bjobs`, `tmux list-sessions`), so the only ways to find out are:

- open a terminal and poll it by hand, or
- keep a monitoring tab open, or
- notice four hours later
that it finished and you never looked.
The GUI already knows which conversation you were working in. `dsh-job-watch` attaches the job id to

that
conversation, queries the provider for you, and paints the conversation's row — so "which conv

ersation still
has something running, and which one finished while I was away" is answered by the si

debar you are already
looking at.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Green is deliberately sticky: it does **not** expire, because it exists to make you come back. It cl

ears the
moment you actually say something in that conversation — and injected context (workspace in

structions, skill
catalogs, runtime snapshots) does not count as "saying something", because that wo

uld clear it silently and
defeat the whole feature.
## Screenshot

> A real screenshot of the sidebar: three tracked conversations, each with the **running** bar
> (`#
ec4899`, the exact colour the plugin paints) on the left edge of its row. The conversation titles ar

e
> covered by a solid block — they are the author's private session names, and the crop is verified

pixel by
> pixel to contain no text at all. No green example appears here simply because no tracked

job had finished
> when the shot was taken; green means "finished, come back and analyse".
## How it works
| Half | Runs in | Does |
| **host** (`lib/index.js`) | the `dsh` process | the job ledger, the provider poller, the `job_watc

h` agent tool, `/api/job-watch/*` |
| **browser** (`lib/client.js`) | the Web GUI | reads the state
endpoint and paints the sidebar rows |
The plugin owns **no** job logic. A *provider* is a shell command plus one regex applied per output

line —
so an HPC scheduler, `tmux` on a bare-metal box, or your own status CLI are all the same thin

g to it.
Nothing about a cluster, queue or path is hard-coded.
Queries happen on four triggers, all of them cheap and skipping each other:
| Trigger | Why it exists |

| every `pollMinutes` (default 30) | the normal rhythm |
| a 60 s heartbeat that compares the wall c
lock against the monotonic clock | a suspended machine freezes timers, so a timer firing "on time" p

roves nothing; clock drift > 90 s is the evidence of a sleep, and the poll catches up right away |
|
opening / refocusing the GUI | you are here, so the state you are shown should be current (the host

only re-queries if the ledger is older than `requestStaleSeconds`) |
| right after `register` | the
colour must be correct immediately, not in 30 minutes |
## Limitations (measured, not guessed)
- **The sidebar has no decoration API.** The browser half finds a row's session id through the React

fiber
chain hanging off the row DOM node and injects the marker into the row. This is inherently ti

ed to the
current sidebar implementation; when it breaks, the console and `window.__dshJobWatch.stat

s()` say so
instead of failing silently.
- **`register` is a manual step** — see above. There is no

way around it for jobs DSH did not spawn.
- **Only rows the sidebar renders get a colour.** A conver

sation that is not in the visible list is not
painted (the rollup is still computed, so it paints as

soon as the row appears).
- **`linePattern` is yours to get right.** A pattern that matches the hea

der row as a job will track a fake
job; a pattern that matches nothing silently tracks nothing (whic

h is why `refresh` reports how many ids
each provider listed).
- **No test of the GUI itself.** `nod

e --test test/kernel.test.mjs` covers the kernel — listing parsing, STAT
folding, the real-prompt di
scriminator, and the finish-time contract.
## Prior art, and what is actually new here
Job *listing* is not new, and none of it is claimed as an idea of this plugin. In the DSH ecosystem:
| Project | What it covers | Why this is different |
| official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-jobs` (the `ui-jobs` entry) | background jobs **DSH itself sp
awned**, in the session header | this is for jobs DSH did **not** start: a scheduler, a tmux session

, another machine |
| `lql341/dsh-scnet` | SCNet HPC as **tools + a skill** (submit, status, logs, c
ancel) | on-demand tool calls for one specific platform; no conversation-level colour, no ETA contra

ct |
| `Gczmy/dsh-node-sched` | a **dashboard** for their own `sched` daemon | requires that daemon;

a main-panel view rather than the conversation list |
| `Luaphes/dsh-web-attention-badge` | **sessi
on** attention state in the browser tab bar (amber = waiting on you, green = done) | a session has f

inished, not a job; painted in the tab strip, not on the conversation row |
| `catsenior507/dsh-comm
and-center` | a panel for running background jobs | a panel you open, not a colour on the row you ar
el for running background jobs | a panel you open, not a colour on the row you are already reading |
The increment claimed here is narrow: **an external job id → a colour on that conversation's sidebar

row**,
plus the finish-time contract (arithmetic or an explicit refusal to guess) and the sleep/wak

e-safe poller.
Everything else — the job tools, the dashboards, the attention badges — belongs to th
erything else — the job tools, the dashboards, the attention badges — belongs to the projects above.
